intro: Sentence-final とも is an emphatic yes. It answers a question or request by confirming it as beyond doubt: "of course!", "certainly!", "you bet!". The core image is a hearty nod: how could you even ask?

skills.rule: End your answer with とも to agree or consent emphatically: "of course", "certainly".
skills.explain:
とも responds. Someone asks a question, makes a request or voices a doubt, and you answer that the thing is obviously so: 手伝ってくれる? / いいとも (sure!), 本当? / 本当だとも (it's true, I swear). It is warm and hearty, with a slightly old-fashioned or fatherly tone; you meet it in stories, from older speakers, and in set replies like いいとも.

Form: plain verbs and い-adjectives take it directly (行くとも, いいとも); nouns and な-adjectives need だ (そうだとも, 大丈夫だとも). It also follows です and ます: そうですとも, 覚えていますとも. It is often reinforced with もちろん or ええ.

The edge is new information and questions. とも confirms something already on the table; it cannot announce news (that is よ) and it cannot ask. Do not confuse it with the とも of 二人とも (both of them) or 少なくとも (at least), which is a different word.
patterns: もちろん [verb] ますとも

examples.jp: あの日[ひ]のことは、よく覚[おぼ]えています{とも}。
examples.en: Of course I remember that day well.

contrast.note: よ hands over new information: 行くよ (I'll go, just so you know). とも confirms in answer, as beyond doubt: 行くとも (of course I'll go!).
ね seeks agreement from the listener: そうですね. とも gives strong agreement to the listener: そうですとも.

mistakes.note: A noun or な-adjective needs だ (or です) before とも.
とも only confirms something already asked or doubted. Announcing news takes よ.

skills.tip: Is it an answer that means "of course, how could you doubt it"? Then とも.
